title: Theo and the Current
premise: Silas Pemberton, a bush pilot who ferries medicine and secrets into the river country, pulls a sealed chest from a flood-swollen current and finds it stamped with the crest of Vessania, a nation erased from every map. The chest carries proof of a massacre the victors paid to forget, and both the old regime's surviving agents and a government inspector want it buried. Stranded by the monsoon with a broken plane, Silas joins forces with Mara Okonjo, a disgraced archivist who has spent her life hunting that proof, and together they run the flooded waterways toward the capital's last free press. Betrayed by an ally, hunted by the inspector who once loved Mara, they must choose between destroying the evidence to save themselves or delivering it at the cost of everything. In the end, Silas trades their beloved plane as a decoy, Mara testifies through the storm, and the truth surfaces—leaving them grounded, exposed, and finally home in each other.
about_author: Wren Thornbury is the pen name of a former river guide turned novelist who lives half the year in a floating cabin on the Kestrel Delta. Their fiction draws on years of hauling supplies upriver for communities the maps forgot.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A routine medicine run ends with Silas fishing a waterlogged chest from a backwater after the flood recedes. The Vessian seal stops them cold—Vessania died twenty years ago. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine, the first crack in a carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Unable to resist, Silas pries the chest open at their airstrip shack: documents, photographs, a ledger of names. Someone is already asking questions on the radio band. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread; the past knocking.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara Okonjo arrives unannounced, having tracked rumors of the chest for a decade. She reveals what the papers prove: the Vessian purge was sanctioned, not accidental. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged over shared obsession.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Weather closes in; the strip will be mud within days. A stranger claiming to be a surveyor scouts the shack, and Silas catches him photographing the chest. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The plane's engine seizes on a test flight—sabotage or bad luck, no way to know. With the air route dead, Mara proposes the river: three hundred miles by boat to the capital. Emotional beat: grief for the plane, resolve taking root.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Reading the ledger aloud, Mara finds her father's name among the disappeared—and Inspector Hale's signature among the authorizing officers. Emotional beat: personal wound fused to public cause.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They buy a leaking longboat from a one-eyed ferryman named Odile and slip onto the brown water as the first monsoon walls arrive. Emotional beat: fragile hope moving fast through hostile country.

chapters.title: The Port of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At a river port, Odile's contacts hide them from a police sweep. Silas learns Mara was expelled from the national archive for asking about Vessania. Emotional beat: intimacy through confession; found family forming around a card game in Odile's back room.

chapters.title: Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The inspector boards a gunboat, torn between duty to bury the chest and his history with Mara. He orders the river locked down but quietly delays the kill order. Emotional beat: love against duty, from the antagonist's side.

chapters.title: Rapids at Night
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Running the Gorge Narrows after dark to dodge checkpoints, the boat nearly founders; Silas saves Mara from the water. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into trust; first unspoken tenderness.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reveals she lost family at Vessania too, and that she's been feeding their position to Hale in exchange for sparing the port. She gives them a head start anyway. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with loyalty; the cost of survival.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Maps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. An old cartographer offers them a hidden channel past the blockade—for the ledger itself. Mara refuses to surrender the original; Silas secretly copies key pages as insurance. Emotional beat: the question of what the truth is worth, and to whom.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Hale's gunboat corners them in the reed marshes. In a tense parley, Hale offers Mara amnesty if she hands over the chest; she refuses, and Silas rams through the cordon, taking a bullet graze. Emotional beat: commitment made irreversible.

chapters.title: Fever Country
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hiding in a stilt village while Silas's wound festers, Mara nurses them and confronts how much she stands to lose beyond the mission. Villagers shelter them despite the risk. Emotional beat: love admitted aloud, quietly, by lamplight.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Gift
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale discovers his superiors plan to sink the gunboat with everyone aboard rather than risk leaks—including him. Shaken, he sends Mara an anonymous warning: the press house is already watched. Emotional beat: the antagonist's defection begins.

chapters.title: City of Rain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the capital under the monsoon's worst, slipping through drowned streets toward the Free Press building, only to find it surrounded. Emotional beat: despair at the threshold; the plan seems dead.

chapters.title: Decoy
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas proposes the unthinkable: repair the old plane, fly it loud and visible across the city as a diversion while Mara goes in on foot. It will mean arrest or worse. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely—the pilot becomes the signal fire.

chapters.title: The Long Way Up
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. While Silas draws the net skyward, Mara climbs through the press house's flooded cellar with the chest on her back, guided by a young printer who owes Odile. Emotional beat: terror and purpose indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Front Page
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. As presses roll and the ledger hits the streets, soldiers breach the doors; Mara reads the names aloud over the broadcast until they take her. Emotional beat: triumph and capture in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ground Fire
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Shot down over the harbor, Silas survives the crash as the story erupts across the city—crowds, strikes, Hale refusing the order to silence witnesses. Emotional beat: wreckage transformed into vindication.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Public inquiry convenes; Hale testifies against his own chain of command, Mara presents the ledger, and the Vessian dead are officially named. Emotional beat: justice outside the law finally entering it.

chapters.title: Still Water
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Months later, Silas and Mara run mail and medicine upriver by boat, the chest enshrined in a new memorial at Odile's port. No more miles instead of years—now there are seasons, shared. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; found family, love, and a life no longer invisible.
